paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Monolingual vs. multilingual datasets over time. While monolingual datasets are more frequent, around 2017 researchers began producing multilingual datasets.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the number of datasets categorized as monolingual or multilingual over time. The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022, with evenly spaced tick labels for each year. The vertical axis is labeled "Number of datasets" and uses a logarithmic scale with a base of 10, ranging from 10 to 10,000.  Four bar groups are arranged for each year, with each group containing two bars representing monolingual (blue) and multilingual (orange) datasets. For the year 2012, the monolingual dataset bar has a height corresponding to approximately 20 datasets, while the multilingual dataset bar reaches approximately 5 datasets. The bar heights for both categories consistently increase from 2013 to 2021, with peaks in 2021, where the monolingual bar reaches approximately 150 datasets and the multilingual bar reaches approximately 80 datasets.  In 2022, the monolingual dataset bar height corresponds to a value of approximately 30 datasets, while the multilingual dataset bar reaches approximately 15 datasets. The bars are not sorted in any specific order other than chronological order by year, and no bars have been visually emphasized.
